nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$, under the uniform distribution on histories of $k$ seeds, that is, on $(\mathbb{F}_2^n)^k$, every history has probability exactly $(2^{nk})^{-1}$. This includes the cases $k = 0$ and $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Uniform mass of a Freivalds seed history

nodes.summary: An $n \times n$ array $A$ of rows over $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2$ determines the $n \times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$ whose $(i, j)$ entry is entry $j$ of row $i$ of $A$.
nodes.title: Matrix of a Freivalds input

nodes.summary: Let $A = B = (1)$ and $C = (0)$ be $1 \times 1$ matrices over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. Then $AB \neq C$.
nodes.title: The sharp Freivalds example has a wrong product

nodes.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2$ and seeds $r_0, \dots, r_{k-1} \in (\mathbb{Z}/2)^n$, the repeated Freivalds test on these seeds accepts if and only if, for every $i < k$, the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$ with seed $r_i$ accepts.
nodes.title: Acceptance of the repeated Freivalds test on fixed seeds

nodes.summary: Let $n, k$ be natural numbers and let $A, B, C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$. The number of histories $(r_1, \dots, r_k)$ of seeds $r_i \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ on which the repeated Freivalds executor accepts equals $a^k$, where $a$ is the number of seeds $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ on which a single Freivalds trial accepts.
nodes.title: Counting accepted histories of repeated Freivalds trials

nodes.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{Z}/2$ with $AB = C$. Then for every $k$, including $k = 0$, and all seeds $r_0, \dots, r_{k-1} \in (\mathbb{Z}/2)^n$, the repeated Freivalds test on these seeds accepts.
nodes.title: Completeness of the repeated Freivalds test on fixed seeds

nodes.summary: For $0 \times 0$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2$ and any number $k$ of seeds (each the empty vector), the repeated Freivalds test accepts and performs no scalar multiplications or additions.
nodes.title: Repeated Freivalds test on empty matrices

nodes.summary: Let $n, k$ be natural numbers and let $A, B, C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$. If the history of $k$ seeds is drawn uniformly from $(\mathbb{F}_2^n)^k$, the probability that the repeated Freivalds executor accepts is $p^k$, where $p$ is the probability that a single Freivalds trial accepts on a seed drawn uniformly from $\mathbb{F}_2^n$.
nodes.title: Acceptance probability of repeated Freivalds trials

nodes.summary: Let $n, k$ be natural numbers and let $A, B, C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with $AB = C$. If the history of $k$ seeds is drawn uniformly from $(\mathbb{F}_2^n)^k$, then the repeated Freivalds executor accepts with probability $1$.
nodes.title: Completeness of repeated Freivalds trials

nodes.summary: Let $A = B = (1)$ and $C = (0)$ be $1 \times 1$ matrices over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, and let $k$ be a natural number. Run $k$ Freivalds trials on $A$, $B$, $C$ with seeds drawn independently and uniformly from $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^1$, accepting exactly when every trial accepts. Then the run accepts with probability exactly $2^{-k}$.
nodes.title: Exact acceptance probability of repeated trials on the sharp Freivalds example

nodes.summary: Let $n, k$ be natural numbers and let $A, B, C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with $AB \ne C$. If the history of $k$ seeds is drawn uniformly from $(\mathbb{F}_2^n)^k$, then the repeated Freivalds executor accepts with probability at most $(2^k)^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Soundness of repeated Freivalds trials

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n, k$ and $n \times n$ matrices $A, B, C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$, this is the probability distribution on $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ of the result returned by the repeated Freivalds executor on $A, B, C$ when its history of $k$ seeds is drawn uniformly from $(\mathbb{F}_2^n)^k$.
nodes.title: Output distribution of repeated Freivalds trials

nodes.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2$ and seeds $r_0, \dots, r_{k-1} \in (\mathbb{Z}/2)^n$, the repeated Freivalds test on these seeds performs exactly $3kn^2$ scalar multiplications and $3kn^2$ scalar additions.
nodes.title: Cost of the repeated Freivalds test on fixed seeds

nodes.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2$, the repeated Freivalds test on the empty list of seeds ($k = 0$) accepts and performs no scalar multiplications or additions.
nodes.title: Repeated Freivalds test with no trials

nodes.summary: Given $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2$ and seeds $r_0, \dots, r_{k-1} \in (\mathbb{Z}/2)^n$, run the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$ with each seed $r_0, \dots, r_{k-1}$ in order, including the trials after a rejection, and return the conjunction of their results (true when $k = 0$). The arithmetic cost of the run is the sum of the costs of the $k$ trials.
nodes.title: Repeated Freivalds test on fixed seeds

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. For every $n$ and every vector $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the uniform probability distribution on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ assigns to $r$ the probability $(2^n)^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Uniform mass of a Freivalds seed

nodes.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and every seed $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$, $r$ returns true if and only if $(AB - C)r = 0$.
nodes.title: Acceptance via the product discrepancy

nodes.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and every seed $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$, $r$ returns true if and only if $A(Br) = Cr$.
nodes.title: Acceptance criterion of the Freivalds trial

nodes.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with $AB \ne C$. Then twice the number of seeds $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ on which the Freivalds trial returns true is at most the number of all seeds in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$; that is, at most half of the seeds accept.
nodes.title: Soundness of the Freivalds trial

nodes.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with $AB = C$. Then for every seed $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$, $r$ returns true. This includes the case $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Completeness of the Freivalds trial

nodes.summary: For $0 \times 0$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and the empty seed $r$, the Freivalds trial returns true at zero cost: it performs no scalar multiplications and no scalar additions.
nodes.title: Freivalds trial on empty matrices

nodes.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, given as arrays. The probability that the Freivalds trial law of $A$, $B$, $C$ returns true equals the number of seeds $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ on which the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$ with seed $r$ accepts, divided by the number $|\mathbb{F}_2^n|$ of all seeds.
nodes.title: Acceptance probability of the Freivalds trial as a seed count

nodes.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, given as arrays. If $AB = C$, then the Freivalds trial law of $A$, $B$, $C$ returns true with probability $1$. This includes the case $n = 0$ of empty matrices.
nodes.title: The Freivalds trial accepts a correct product with probability one

nodes.summary: Let $A = B = (1)$ and $C = (0)$ be $1 \times 1$ matrices over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. When the seed is drawn uniformly from $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^1$, the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$ accepts with probability exactly $1/2$.
nodes.title: The sharp Freivalds example is accepted with probability one half

nodes.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, given as arrays. If $AB \ne C$, then the Freivalds trial law of $A$, $B$, $C$ returns true with probability at most $1/2$.
nodes.title: The Freivalds trial accepts a wrong product with probability at most one half

nodes.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, given as arrays, the Freivalds trial law is the probability distribution on $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ of the value returned by the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$ with seed $r$, where $r$ is drawn uniformly from $\mathbb{F}_2^n$.
nodes.title: Freivalds trial law

nodes.summary: Let $A = B = (1)$ and $C = (0)$ be $1 \times 1$ matrices over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. For every seed $r \in (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^1$, the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$ with seed $r$, which compares $A(Br)$ with $Cr$, accepts if and only if the single entry $r_0$ of $r$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The sharp Freivalds example accepts exactly the zero seed

nodes.summary: Let $A = B = (1)$ and $C = (0)$ be $1 \times 1$ matrices over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. Exactly one seed $r \in (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^1$ is accepted by the Freivalds trial on $A$, $B$, $C$.
nodes.title: The sharp Freivalds example has exactly one accepted seed

nodes.summary: For $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and every seed $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the Freivalds trial performs exactly $3n^2$ scalar multiplications and exactly $3n^2$ scalar additions.
nodes.title: Cost of the Freivalds trial

nodes.summary: Given $n \times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2$, stored as arrays of rows, and a seed $r \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the trial computes the column vectors $Br$, $A(Br)$ and $Cr$, each by accumulating matrix products into a zero column, and returns true exactly when $A(Br) = Cr$. Its cost is the pair (number of scalar multiplications, number of scalar additions), each multiply-add step counting…

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
